description: Solar Parker is a technology-driven team passionate about Earth science, artificial intelligence, and environmental intelligence. We aim to transform NASA Earth observation data into meaningful insights through data analysis, statistical trend detection, interactive visualizations, and AI-powered explanations. Our interests include web development, machine learning, climate analysis, and building innovative solutions for understanding Earth's changing systems.
summary:
EARTHSCOPE AI is an AI-assisted Earth observation and climate trend analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”

The platform helps users investigate environmental trends, compare geographical regions, and understand long-term changes through interactive data exploration and statistical analysis.

It retrieves meteorological observations through the NASA POWER API, enabling users to explore historical patterns, compare regions, identify statistically significant trends, and generate scientific reports with supporting visualisations.

The platform applies statistical methods, including Sen's slope estimation and the Seasonal Mann-Kendall test, to assess trend direction and significance while distinguishing meaningful changes from natural variability. It also includes clearly labelled demonstration datasets inspired by other Earth observation missions and scientific products.

By combining NASA data, statistical methods, interactive visualisations, and AI-assisted interpretation, EARTHSCOPE AI aims to make complex Earth system information more accessible and help users investigate environmental changes using scientific evidence.
details:
EARTHSCOPE AI – Project Details

EARTHSCOPE AI is an AI-driven platform for exploring Earth observation data and analysing climate trends. It brings together data discovery, statistical analysis, regional comparison, AI-assisted interpretation, and scientific reporting in one interactive platform.

1. Find Data

Users can explore different environmental data types, select time periods, and choose geographical locations based on the variables they want to investigate. The meteorological observations used in the current live analysis workflow are retrieved through the NASA POWER API.

2. Analyse Trends

The platform applies statistical methods, including Sen's slope estimation and the Seasonal Mann-Kendall test, to detect and examine environmental trends. These methods help determine the direction of a trend and whether the observed changes are statistically significant.

3. Compare Across Locations

Users can compare environmental trends across different geographical locations. This helps them explore regional differences and understand how environmental patterns vary between locations.

4. AI Scientist

The AI Scientist feature helps users understand analytical results and ask questions about environmental patterns. A deterministic fallback is also available when an external language model is not configured.

5. Explore Data

The platform provides interactive dashboards, trend charts, geographical comparisons, and downloadable PDF reports containing analytical findings and visualisations.

6. Technologies Used

  • Frontend: Next.js, React.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI.
  • Data Source: NASA POWER API.
  • Statistical Analysis: Python.
  • Visualisation: Recharts.
  • PDF Reporting: ReportLab.

7. Data Transparency

The current implementation uses one verified live data source: the NASA POWER API. Six additional datasets have been created as calibrated demonstration datasets inspired by other Earth observation missions and scientific products. These datasets demonstrate the platform's analytical capabilities but are not live mission API integrations. The platform clearly labels demonstration data to distinguish it from verified live observations.

8. Creativity and Impact

EARTHSCOPE AI combines environmental data retrieval, statistical analysis, geographical comparison, AI-assisted interpretation, and scientific reporting in a single accessible platform. It aims to help students, researchers, and other users explore Earth system trends and understand environmental changes through evidence-based analysis.

The platform does not interpret statistical associations as proof of causation. It aims to make Earth observation data easier to explore while maintaining transparency about statistical uncertainty, data sources, and limitations.
